title: [I08:E02] GitNexus: reach from symbol evidence, a roster of trees to index, and rules that each state one invariant
body:
## Summary

The cross-graph reach run settles each member's reach from the two instruments that read symbols — the member's own graph edges, and a search of its tree — with what the registry declares the member consumes the home as carried beside it. A roster states which trees carry a graph, one run walks it and another names what it misses. The rules of the namespace each state one invariant, and the canon gains the two tests that would have caught what this work found by hand.

## What happens today

**Reach conflates a coupling with a reference.** Reach settles from the first instrument that holds, and the first asked is the group's contract registry. A registry link says the member's package manifest depends on the tree the concern lives in — independent of the concern, identical for every symbol that tree publishes. Of six members of a library-and-consumers group, four settled on the registry, and their symbol evidence ranged from thirty-five files down to a single migration guide. All four reported the same reach. A second route into the same conflation sat in the tree search, where a hit on a package name settled the same verdict a declared link already carried.

**A probe reads one of the three answers its question returns.** The probe addresses a boundary name in another member's graph, where it has no symbol identity to pass. An ambiguous name answers with candidates and an undefined one with a not-found error; the run read only the single-report shape, so two of three answers bound a field they do not carry.

**A judgement declares a value its own protocol overwrites.** A member with neither a graph nor a tree is recorded `unanswerable`; the phase that settles reach afterwards ran over every member and read that member's absent probe and absent search as "neither found one".

**Which trees carry a graph is decided by whoever last ran a build.** Nothing states the set, so a tree with no graph and a tree nobody thought to index look identical. A repository group written in May still listed the components indexed that afternoon; three added to the superproject the following week were absent four months later, and the one holding key handling was among them. Bringing a tree up to date has a second gap: the pin refuses a working tree carrying modifications, and the trees under a code-intelligence tool are exactly the trees that tool writes into.

**Rules carry procedure and several invariants at once.** Rules on the namespace's shared contract and on its build operation open or close on instructions — "Index each tree whose answers a caller will ask for by name", "Record which graph an answer came from" — which a container that runs no Protocol has no step to hold. Four hold several constraints under one name, so no part can be cited or edited without the rest: one carries its second rule as a bolded sentence-lede, another runs to 381 words against a next-largest of 212.

**The canon cannot see either defect this work found by hand.** A rule cited by a slug its reader's ancestry does not carry is well-formed, declared, and names nothing that arrived — and the entry governing citation form tests only spellings and citations declared nowhere. An output admitting a value no protocol path leaves standing passes every existing test too.

## The fix

**Reach from symbol evidence, the dependency as its own reading.** Reach is `graph` where a definition the probe found carries a dependent, `hand-derived` where the tree search found a boundary symbol, `none` where both instruments were asked and neither found one, `unanswerable` where the member has neither to ask, and `home` for the member the concern was raised in. The settling phase runs only over members with an instrument to ask, so the unanswerable member keeps that reading. A second field records the registry's cross-link, which lets the judgement name two readings it could not express: a declared consumer holding no reference, and a member whose tree names a boundary package the links never declared.

**The probe reads every shape its question returns**, recording each definition with the file it sits in, which separates a mirror of the home's symbol from a homonym.

**A roster names the trees, and one run walks it.** `roster-refresh` gives each tree a graph where none covers it and brings the graph current where it trails, composing the git library's `ready-checkouts` so one invocation moves every checkout to its named revision first. `reset-checkout` returns a tree to what its repository records and answers what it discarded, read before the reset runs because afterwards nothing else says what the tree held. `component-scan` reads what the host declares as submodules and names the components no roster entry covers — reporting only, because an entry carries a decision and a reason that a path comparison supplies neither of.

**Each rule states one invariant, as a fact.** Nine entries on the shared contract where there were five, three on the build operation where there was one, each named for what it asserts. Prohibitions keep their negative framing, which is the sanctioned shape; what goes is the imperative naming a step's work. Citers move to the half each means, and two citation lengths are corrected — four written at full length inside the namespace that declares the rule, and one written bare in a workflow that inherits nothing from it.

**The canon gains both tests.** The citation-form entry's Detect now resolves each slug against the rules the loader merges into the citing technique. `unproducible-declared-value` walks the values an output enumerates and asks which phase leaves each standing when the run ends. The principle behind both is widened from operations to rules.

## Scope

The gitnexus and git library namespaces, the conformance specimen, and two canon resources. No engine change, no schema change.

## What was verified

The full corpus guard sweep passes, 49 of 49, on the combined tree.

The specimen was walked twice on the experiment sidecar over a six-member group of a library and its consumers, after a minimum viable workflow held on the instance. A claim table was written first and the protocol paper-walked against the live group before the sidecar was touched — which is where the probe-shape defect was found, for the cost of two calls rather than a full walk. The first walk took a concern two consumers never name and produced the two outcomes the design exists to separate; the second took a concern every consumer names and produced the undeclared coupling. All three probe answer shapes appeared. `unanswerable` has no subject in that group and is recorded unevidenced rather than shown.

`unanswerable` stays unevidenced across all three walks: every member of the group has both a graph and a tree, so the value has no subject to take. The correction to the settling phase is what makes it reachable at all, and this fixture cannot show that.

The settings file beside a tree was confirmed to set a build's defaults: a build invoked with no flag reported the mode changing because the file pinned it, and the trees rebuilt under that pin came back carrying layers they did not hold before — one of them at four times the nodes.

The readiness gate has not been walked end to end. Its survey, its decision and its reset were each established against live checkouts, but no run has taken the three in sequence.

The reset semantics were established against live checkouts before the operation was written: seventeen components surveyed, four carrying modifications the code-intelligence tool had written into their tracked files and one carrying nested checkouts off the commits it records. A reset over tracked paths and nested positions returned all seventeen to pristine, and the untracked configuration pinned beside each tree survived it — the property `an-untracked-file-survives-a-reset` states. The coverage judgement was walked by hand over the same superproject: twenty-two declared submodules against twenty-two roster entries, nothing uncovered, two paths marked infrastructure.

A third walk took the combined tree, over the same group, against a concern in the home's key handling. It is the sharpest evidence for the separation, because the two columns disagree everywhere: all five consumers settle `hand-derived`, each from a search of its own tree, while four carry a declared link and the fifth carries none. Under the reading this change replaces, the four would have settled on their links and the fifth on a package name, and every row would have read alike.

Every probe came back not-found, which is the shape a consumer's graph gives for a name it imports — the graph holds a node for what a tree defines and none for what it consumes, so the tree search is what answers and the run records it as such rather than as a blank. The home probe came back ambiguous between a struct and its implementation block, which is the case the run's symbol-identity input exists for. The route and tool reads over a Rust crate both answered empty, each recorded as an instrument asked rather than a question skipped. The member the group's links do not declare is the one the merged ranking surfaced, and two members whose trees carry the concern were surfaced by nothing.

The rule changes were served on the sidecar rather than only guarded, because guards read files while the loader composes them. On the combined tree every rule of the namespace arrives under the shared contract as its own entry, once; the build operation's three arrive inlined with its step; the repointed citations resolve to the new names inside the delivered bodies; and the build operation's citation of a container rule arrives in the same delivery as that rule's declaration. Reading that composed contract is also what found the last imperative — a verb outside the list a static sweep was matching on.

Both canon tests were run against the instances that prompted them and against their near misses. The citation test flags the namespace rule cited bare from a workflow inheriting nothing from it and passes it cited bare from four techniques inside. The declared-value test flags the judgement whose settling phase ran over every member and passes it once that phase is scoped.

## Non-goals

No GitNexus engine change, and no change to the single-graph operations. No scheduled or daemonised refresh, and no change to what a repository group holds — a group definition is authored, not derived. The scan does not edit the roster it measures. No guard for either new canon test, though both are mechanisable. The registry's completeness is still bounded by the links an operator declares; this makes that boundary legible rather than removing it.
